abstract:
Maternal transmission of the APP transgene lowers amyloid burden in 5xFAD mice. We examined whether APPPS1-21 shows a similar parent-of-origin association and whether Thy1.2 methylation contributes. F1 offspring inheriting the transgene from the mother had less A{beta}42, fewer plaques, less gliosis, and less human APP at intermediate ages. The A{beta}42 difference was not detected in the F2 cohort at 100 days. Non-transgenic off-spring of APPPS1 mothers did not differ in glial counts, and serum anti-A{beta} antibody levels were not higher at 40 days. In an exploratory methylation analysis of 32 brains, parent-of-origin-associated differences were sex-specific and enriched on chromosome X, not chromosome 2. The Thy1.2-APP cassette showed an approximately three-percentage-point paternal increase; the PSEN1 cassette did not. These findings establish an association with parental transmission but do not show that methylation causes the pathology differences.

IN BRIEFWe report lower amyloid pathology after F0 maternal APPPS1 transmission to F1. The A{beta}42 difference was not detected in the F2 cohort. The small Thy1.2-APP methylation difference does not establish a causal mechanism.
